**Solution 3 is the correct one.** I checked its chain of reasoning independently, though I did not run numerics here.

- **Reduction.** The plateau potential is \(-\varepsilon^2+\tfrac14\operatorname{sech}^2 s\), and the walls rise to 144. So \(\lambda_\varepsilon=k^2-\varepsilon^2\) with \(k\) set by a quantization condition on a well of width \(\sim\pi/\varepsilon\). This gives \(a=3\), so Solution 2's \(a=-1\) is wrong. Its evenness argument also fails, since \(L_\varepsilon\sim\pi/(2\varepsilon)\) is odd in \(\varepsilon\).

- **Even ground state.** The zero-energy solutions of \(f''=\tfrac14\operatorname{sech}^2 s\,f\) are \(\tfrac{2}{\pi}[K(k)\pm K(k')]\) with \(k^2=1/(1+e^{2s})\). This gives intercepts \(m_e=2\ln2+\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) (even) and \(m_o=2\ln2-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) (odd). Since \(m_o<m_e\), the odd mode has the larger \(k\), so the even mode is the ground state. Solution 1 uses the odd mode, which is the wrong one.

- **Plateau length.** The even solution of the linearized equation is \(F\sim R\cos(\varepsilon s-\sum_{j=1}^6\arctan(\varepsilon/j))\), which follows from the reflectionless Pöschl–Teller phase. Its first large zero is \(L_\varepsilon=\pi/(2\varepsilon)+H_6+O(\varepsilon)\) with \(H_6=49/20\). Solution 1's \(q=-51/20\) disagrees with this.

- **Wall offset.** \(g=e^{-\nu\xi}Z_\varepsilon'\) solves \(g''=(144-pZ^{p-1})g\) exactly. Matching gives \(S=L+\theta_1\), and the zero of \(g\) sits at \(\xi_0=-\theta_1-1/\nu\) with \(\nu=6\). So the effective wall is at \(S+\xi_0=L-\tfrac16\), and \(\theta_1\) cancels.

- **Quantization.** \(k(\pi/(2\varepsilon)+\tfrac{137}{60}+m_e)=\pi+o(1)\), which gives \(\lambda_\varepsilon=3\varepsilon^2-\tfrac{16}{\pi}\bigl(\tfrac{137}{60}+2\ln2+\tfrac{\pi}{2}\bigr)\varepsilon^3+\dots\). Hence \(b=-8-\tfrac{32\ln2}{\pi}-\tfrac{548}{15\pi}\approx-26.689\), matching Solution 3.

CHOICE: 3
